chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ghiyath ibn Ibrahim, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him),
that he disliked the julahiq (pellet bow/sling).

key_terms.الْجُلَاهِقَ: Julahiq — a type of pellet bow, sling, or stone-throwing device; using it to hunt is considered makruh because the animal may die from the impact rather than from a lawful slaughter
key_terms.كَرِهَ: Disliked, disapproved — in fiqh terminology, karaha indicates a discouraged but not strictly forbidden action (makruh)

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible (halal) to hunt using a julahiq (pellet bow or sling) in Islamic law?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) expressed disapproval (karaha) of the julahiq, a type of pellet-launching device or sling used in hunting. In Islamic jurisprudence, karaha typically indicates that an action is discouraged but not strictly forbidden; here, the Imam's disapproval of this hunting implement likely relates to its inability to ensure a clean, permissible kill — as game killed by blunt or pellet projectiles may die from the impact rather than from a lawful slaughter method. This ruling is part of the broader jurisprudential discussion about which weapons and methods are permissible for hunting game.
